text: Write a program showing that generics are erased. Fill in the three blanks.
explanation: Verified: `true` and `java.util.ArrayList`. There is no class `ArrayList<String>` at run time — the compiler checks the type argument, inserts casts, and removes it. So generics are a compile-time discipline over an untyped runtime, and the guarantee is conditional: if your code compiled without unchecked warnings, the inserted casts will never fail.
